results.title: KIVI: A Tuning-Free Asymmetric 2bit Quantization for KV Cache
results.content:
Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated strong performance across a wide range of tasks (Brown et al., 2020; Taylor et al., 2022; Yuan et al., 2023; Chuang et al., 2024).
However, their deployment is very costly, requiring a large number of hardware accelerators such as GPUs.
Given these substantial costs, one natural way to reduce the cost per request is to combine a sufficient number of requests together for batch processing. [...] Efficiently serving large language models (LLMs) requires batching of many requests to reduce the cost per request. Yet, with larger batch sizes and longer context lengths, the key-value (KV) cache, which stores attention keys and values to avoid re-computations, significantly increases memory demands and becomes the new bottleneck in speed and memory usage. Additionally, the loading of the KV cache causes the computational core to be idle, which limits the inference speed. [...] A new plug-and-play 2bit KV cache quantization algorithm without any fine-tuning, KIVI, with hardware-friendly implementation.
We conduct an extensive evaluation for KIVI with Llama, Mistral, and Falcon on popular generation tasks.
KIVI can efficiently compress KV cache to 2bit and bring 2.6×\mathbf{2.6\times} peak memory usage reduction for Llama-2-7B, with little to no accuracy drop.

KIVI is a new plug-and-play 2bit KV cache quantization algorithm without any fine-tuning. This algorithm optimizes memory usage by quantizing the key cache per-channel and the value cache per-token to 2bit. KIVI's hardware-friendly design allows LLMs like Llama-2, Falcon, and Mistral to maintain comparable quality levels while reducing peak memory usage by 2.6 times. This enables up to 4 times larger batch sizes and significantly increases throughput by 2.35 to 3.47 times in real LLM inference [...] ```

results.title: TurboQuant vs KIVI: KV Cache Quantization Compared | TurboQuant Tools
results.content:
KIVI

Distribution-aware KV quantization: per-channel quantization for keys and per-token quantization for values.

## What the papers emphasize

TurboQuant

Google highlights zero-accuracy-loss-style benchmark claims, at least 6x KV footprint reduction on long-context tasks, and up to 8x faster attention-logit computation on H100.

KIVI [...] ## Which one looks stronger on paper

TurboQuant

### TurboQuant looks stronger if quality retention is the priority

Google's paper emphasizes low-distortion inner-product estimation, long-context quality, and benchmark parity near the 3 to 4-bit operating range.

KIVI

### KIVI looks stronger if simplicity and 2-bit cache reduction are the priority

KIVI is easier to reason about as a KV-only quantization baseline and is commonly referenced when teams want a direct 2-bit comparison point. [...] KIVI

The KIVI paper highlights around 2.6x lower peak memory including weights, up to 4x larger batch size, and 2.35x–3.47x throughput gains on real inference workloads.

## What changes between the two methods

TurboQuant and KIVI both target KV cache memory, but they optimize for different points on the accuracy, complexity, and compression tradeoff curve. TurboQuant adds more math to reduce distortion; KIVI keeps the method simpler and more directly tied to 2-bit cache compression.

results.title: KIVI: A Tuning-Free Asymmetric 2bit Quantization for KV Cache [Quick Review]
results.content:
+ KIVI, a tuning-free asymmetric 2-bit quantization method, consistently outperforms other 2-bit quantization configurations by quantizing key cache per-channel and value cache per-token. This approach maintains accuracy close to the 16-bit baseline across various LLMs (Llama-2, Mistral, Falcon) and generation tasks (CoQA, TruthfulQA, GSM8K, LongBench), demonstrating its effectiveness in preserving model quality while significantly reducing memory footprint. For instance, on Llama-2-7B, [...] Efficiently serving large language models necessitates batching many requests, yet increased batch sizes and context lengths make KV cache a significant memory and speed bottleneck.
 Quantization can reduce KV cache size, but a lack of in-depth studies exists on its element distribution, hindering effective quantization strategies.
 This research aims to analyze KV cache element distribution in LLMs to identify optimal quantization approaches and overcome current limitations. [...] Quick review
